title: Preeclampsia: intrarenal vasospasm causing oliguria
vignette: A 31-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, at 30 weeks gestation comes to the emergency department due to increased swelling in her face and lower extremities. She has noticed a sudden onset of swelling and a 2.72-kg (6-lb) weight gain in the last day. The patient has not urinated in the last 12 hours despite an increase in fluid intake. She has a twin pregnancy and no chronic medical conditions. Blood pressure is 154/98 mm Hg, and pulse is 98/min. Bladder catheterization yields a total of 10 mL of dark urine. Urinalysis shows no red blood cells. Which of the following pathologic factors is the most likely cause of this patient's decreased urine output?

clues.text: increased swelling in her face and lower extremities
clues.note: New facial and extremity edema with rapid weight gain in the third trimester suggests preeclampsia (capillary leak from endothelial injury).
Twin (multifetal) gestation increases placental mass and is a major risk factor for preeclampsia.
New-onset hypertension (>=140/90) at >=20 weeks gestation with end-organ signs defines preeclampsia.

clues.text: Urinalysis shows no red blood cells
clues.note: Oliguria WITHOUT red cells/casts argues against glomerulonephritis and points to a PRE-glomerular (vascular) cause - intrarenal vasospasm.

whatMatters: Third-trimester new hypertension + edema + oliguria in a twin pregnancy = PREECLAMPSIA. The ischemic placenta releases antiangiogenic factors that damage maternal endothelium, causing widespread VASOSPASM. Intrarenal arterial vasospasm reduces renal blood flow and GFR -> oliguria (concentrated urine, no RBCs). Answer E.
strategy: Diagnose preeclampsia (>=20 weeks: new hypertension + end-organ dysfunction), then trace the oliguria: diffuse endothelial injury -> VASOSPASM -> decreased renal perfusion/GFR. The absence of RBCs/casts excludes glomerular inflammation. Reject glomerular inflammation/immune-complex deposition (would show hematuria/casts), interstitial nephritis (drug-related, rash/fever), and an obstructing stone (unilateral, hematuria - and one kidney compensates).

options.text: Obstructing stone within the renal calyx

eliminations.label: Inflammation of the glomeruli - would show hematuria/casts
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: glomerulonephritis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it typically causes hematuria with RBC casts; this patient's urinalysis shows NO red cells, and the clinical picture is preeclampsia-driven vasospasm. ✅ Correct if: nephritic urine with dysmorphic RBCs/casts.

eliminations.label: Immune complex deposition - glomerulonephritis (lupus/IgA)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: immune-complex glomerulonephritis (e.g., lupus, IgA). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it produces proteinuria WITH hematuria/casts, not the RBC-negative oliguria of preeclamptic vasospasm. ✅ Correct if: immune-complex glomerular disease with active urine sediment.

eliminations.label: Inflammation of the renal interstitium - drug-related AIN
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: acute interstitial nephritis (often from NSAIDs/antibiotics) with fever, rash, eosinophils. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: no offending drug or hypersensitivity features here; the cause is preeclamptic vasospasm. ✅ Correct if: drug exposure + rash/fever + WBC casts/eosinophiluria.

eliminations.label: Obstructing stone - unilateral, other kidney compensates
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a calculus obstructing one kidney. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it usually causes hematuria and unilateral obstruction, with the contralateral kidney maintaining output; it doesn't explain systemic hypertension/edema. ✅ Correct if: renal colic with hematuria and hydronephrosis.

reasoning: New hypertension + edema + oliguria at 30 weeks in a twin pregnancy = preeclampsia
The ischemic placenta releases antiangiogenic factors that injure maternal endothelium
Diffuse vasospasm reduces renal blood flow and GFR -> oliguria (RBC-negative, concentrated urine)
-> vasospasm of the intrarenal arteries; answer E
mechanism: Preeclampsia is new-onset HYPERTENSION (>=140/90) at >=20 weeks gestation plus proteinuria and/or signs of end-organ dysfunction. It arises from abnormal placentation with poorly remodeled spiral arteries and placental ISCHEMIA (risk is higher with increased placental mass, e.g., TWIN gestation). The ischemic placenta releases ANTIANGIOGENIC factors (e.g., soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1) that cause widespread maternal ENDOTHELIAL cell damage. Two consequences follow: (1) capillary leak -> third-spacing of fluid (facial/extremity edema, rapid weight gain) and proteinuria, and (2) loss of endothelial control of vascular tone -> systemic VASOSPASM with end-organ hypoperfusion. In the KIDNEYS, intrarenal arterial vasospasm reduces renal blood flow and glomerular filtration rate, producing OLIGURIA with minimal, concentrated urine and rising creatinine - without hematuria (no glomerular inflammation). Definitive treatment is delivery of the placenta. The distractors (glomerular inflammation, immune-complex deposition, interstitial nephritis, obstructing stone) would show active urine sediment or a different clinical context.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Repro > preeclampsia: new hypertension >=20 wk + proteinuria/end-organ damage; placental ischemia -> antiangiogenic factors -> endothelial injury -> vasospasm + capillary leak; delivery is curative.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Oliguria with NO RBCs in preeclampsia = renal (pre-glomerular) vasospasm, not glomerulonephritis.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on preeclampsia, vasospasm, antiangiogenic factors (sFlt-1), oliguria, or nephritic sediment? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Glomerular inflammation/immune complexes = hematuria/casts; interstitial nephritis = drug/rash; stone = unilateral/hematuria.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: preeclampsia -> endothelial damage -> vasospasm (hypertension, renal hypoperfusion/oliguria) + capillary leak (edema/proteinuria); treat by delivery.

keywords.front: New hypertension + edema + oliguria at >=20 weeks

keywords.back: Intrarenal arterial vasospasm (reduced renal blood flow/GFR)
Placental ischemia -> antiangiogenic factors -> endothelial injury

keywords.front: Preeclampsia risk factor in this case

firstAid.detail: Repro: endothelial injury -> vasospasm; renal hypoperfusion -> oliguria; capillary leak -> edema/proteinuria.
OB > BP control, magnesium for seizure prophylaxis; delivery is curative.

memoryHook: The sick placenta poisons mom's blood vessels - they clamp down (vasospasm), the kidneys get squeezed dry (oliguria), and fluid leaks into her face and legs.
